# agent-reflex plugin

An OpenCode plugin that adds a small System One decision model (Jev, nimble, d1,
liquid-d1...) as a classifier to the agent loop. This skill briefs the user on
its capabilities and installs or updates it. The installer also installs the
Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Qwen Code, Antigravity, Pi and MiMo Code ports when
their CLIs are present.

## Locate the installer

When this skill runs from the repository, the installer is at
`../../../install.sh` relative to this skill's directory, the README at
`../../../README.md`, example configs at `../../../opencode.example.jsonc`,
the source at `../../../plugins/opencode/index.ts`.

When this skill was installed standalone (e.g. via
`npx skills add psygreg/agent-reflex`), the repository is not present: clone
it first and use `<clone>/install.sh` instead:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/psygreg/agent-reflex /tmp/agent-reflex
```

## Requirement

The plugin needs a System One decision model as its classifier, served at
`<baseURL>/systemone`: local llama.cpp (0.6+)/Ollama (0.35+)/LM Studio
(0.4.26+), or TypeSafe's Jev through the TypeSafe API, OpenRouter, the Vercel
AI Gateway or OpenCode Zen. A `fallbackModel` option retries the classifier when
the primary model rejects requests (e.g. a free-model window closing). Every
capability below is driven by this classifier.

## Capabilities (brief the user with this)

- **Decision-driven history compaction**: when the history grows long, the
  recent messages are kept verbatim (a keep-window that widens with the task's
  complexity), the most load-bearing older messages are kept too (bounded, so a
  long session cannot preserve its whole tail), and the rest are folded into a
  compact structured digest of the facts they established — so detail is
  compressed rather than discarded. Structural messages (tool calls/results) are
  scored like any other and only survive when load-bearing.
- **Complexity classification**: every prompt is scored *simple*, *medium* or
  *high*; `maxTokens` is set per level and medium/high prompts get a system
  note suggesting a confidence check before committing to a solution.
- **Automatic effort control**: when the agent has no non-default model variant
  or explicit effort setting, the classified level is written into each primary
  request in the dialect the requested model actually speaks, and sets the
  matching `maxTokens` cap. User-selected variants and effort settings take
  precedence. Wired dialects:
  Claude (`output_config.effort`), GPT reasoning models (`reasoning.effort` /
  `reasoning_effort`), GLM-5.2+ (`thinking.type` + `reasoning_effort`), Xiaomi
  MiMo V2.5+ (`thinking.type`, or `reasoning.effort` / `reasoning_effort` on
  the Responses API and gateway routes), Google Gemini 3+ (`thinkingLevel`, or
  `reasoning_effort` on OpenAI-compatible routes), Qwen 3.5+ / qwen-plus /
  qwen-max (`enable_thinking` + `reasoning_effort` on Chat Completions,
  `reasoning.effort` on Responses, `thinking.type` + `output_config.effort` on
  the Anthropic surface), Moonshot Kimi 2.7+/K3 (`reasoning_effort` on K3,
  `thinking.type` toggle on K2.7/K2.6), xAI Grok 4.3+ (`reasoning_effort`, or
  `reasoning.effort` on Responses; `none` disables on grok-4.3 only, `xhigh`
  tops out on grok-4.3/4.6+), MiniMax M3+ (`thinking.type: adaptive` stays on
  for MiniMax-M3 agent turns because disabling it can yield empty responses;
  `reasoning_effort` / `output_config.effort` tunes M3.1-Flash, and
  `reasoning.effort` is used on Responses; `none` is rejected), local
  llama.cpp/Ollama (`reasoning_effort`, plus `chat_template_kwargs` on llama.cpp). Dialects are
  detected per request, so multimodel setups never send a foreign field;
  models without a wired dialect stay untouched.
- **Confidence tool**: the `systemone_check_confidence` tool scores the
  model's current line of thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.
- **Tool exposure**: for each prompt the classifier decides which tool *groups*
  the task needs (tools are judged by purpose — web, shell, edit, read, agents,
  other — one question per group, not per tool) and the model is given only
  those, so the request carries fewer tool schemas and saves input tokens; a
  kept group keeps its whole family of tools. The always-keep set is the common
  core (read/search/edit/shell/task) plus `reflex_run` and
  `systemone_check_confidence`, so the model can always follow the confidence
  guidance on complex tasks. Only the long tail (web, exec, subagents…) is
  trimmed to what the task clearly needs or the model already used this session.
  Everything is exposed if the classifier is unavailable. If filtering hides a
  needed tool, `systemone_reveal_tools` lists the agent's tool pool and restores
  all its schemas for the current user request.
  OpenCode batches complexity, tool-relevance, and compaction-relevance decisions
  per user request and reuses them across tool continuations; history-relevance
  verdicts persist for the whole session, so each old message is judged by the
  classifier at most once. Parallel safety/edit checks share a batch when their
  hooks arrive together. Sequential safety and edit checks remain per action
  because their inputs are only available then.
- **Tool dispatch** (`reflex_run`): an optional fallback tool for when the model
  cannot decide which underlying tool a task needs. It asks the decision model
  which tool to use (a `choice` decision), runs it, and returns its real output.
  The model calls tools directly whenever it already knows which one fits and
  reaches for `reflex_run` only when the correct tool is unclear. The shell
  guardrail runs before dispatch. Tool dispatch uses the same configured
  classifier model as the rest of the plugin.
- **Shell guardrail**: shell commands are scored for damage potential;
  dangerous ones are denied.
- **Syntax checks**: after `edit`/`write` the file is checked with language
  parsers (plus a classifier bug check on medium/high), with one retry and
  then an ask-the-user stop.
- **Project agent-docs nudge**: on a conversation's initial prompt the plugin
  checks the repository root for agent guidance (`AGENTS.md` or a `.ai/`
  directory) and, when one exists, injects a one-line note telling the model
  to read it before starting the task — once per conversation, never re-fed
  on later prompts (OpenCode only).

Which features actually reach the agent — and with what caveat — is per agent:
see the support table below.

## Agent support

Eight agents are supported: OpenCode (the reference) plus the ports below. The
same features run in Claude Code (`plugins/claude-code`), Codex
(`plugins/codex`), Hermes (`plugins/hermes`), Qwen Code (`plugins/qwen-code`),
Antigravity (`plugins/antigravity`), Pi (`plugins/pi`) and MiMo Code
(`plugins/mimocode`), which the installer sets up when each CLI is
present. The classifier config is shared (`agent-reflex.jsonc`, same option
names), so the user answers the classifier questions once.

Which features reach each agent — and with what caveat — is in the table below.
Dynamic effort needs the plugin to rewrite the model request, and history
compaction needs it to rewrite the message list — both only reach agents whose hook
API allows that rewrite. OpenCode, Pi and MiMo Code all share the same
decision-driven compaction (Pi and MiMo Code gate it behind `AGENT_REFLEX_PRUNE=1`):

| Agent | Guardrail | Post-edit checks | Compaction guidance | Dynamic effort | History compaction | Tool exposure | Tool dispatch | Key caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | hard block | inline | built-in | full (per-model dialects) | decision-driven | yes | yes (`reflex_run`) | Reference implementation; everything works. |
| Pi | hard block | inline | via `context` | full (`setThinkingLevel`) | opt-in decision-driven | yes (`setActiveTools`) | yes (`reflex_run`) | Pi translates the effort level per model itself. |
| MiMo Code | hard block | inline | compacting hook | token cap only | opt-in decision-driven | no | no | `chat.params` has `maxTokens` but no `reasoning_effort`. |
| Claude Code | hard block | inline | fact-extraction guidance | no | digest guidance only | no | no | `PreCompact` extracts fact buckets from the transcript to steer the summary, but cannot rewrite the message list. |
| Qwen Code | hard block | inline | fact-extraction guidance | no | digest guidance only | no | no | Same hook limits as Claude Code. |
| Codex | hard block | inline | inert | no | no | no | no | Compaction hook can only cancel compaction; edits via `apply_patch` (V4A). |
| Antigravity | hard block | one turn late | inert | no | no | no | no | `PostToolUse` cannot inject context (antigravity-cli#808). |
| Hermes | wrapper tool | inline | none | no | no | no | no | Hooks cannot block a tool call; guardrail is a `safe_run` wrapper. |

When installing or updating, tell the user which caveats apply to their agent and
point them at the port's own README (`plugins/<agent>/README.md`) for details.

## Updating an existing installation

`install.sh` detects an existing installation (plugin copy or config entry)
**before asking anything**, so updating needs no answers. Run it with stdin
closed:

```sh
bash ../../../install.sh </dev/null
```

- Only the agent-port plugin files are refreshed: the Claude Code plugin
  files under `~/.claude/plugins/agent-reflex/`, the Codex plugin files
  under `~/.codex/plugins/agent-reflex/`, the Hermes plugin files under
  `~/.hermes/plugins/agent-reflex/`, the Qwen Code extension files under
  `~/.qwen/extensions/agent-reflex/`, the Antigravity plugin files under
  `~/.gemini/config/plugins/agent-reflex/`, the Pi extension files under
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/agent-reflex/`, and the MiMo Code hook files
  under `~/.config/mimocode/hooks/` and `~/.config/mimocode/tools/` — and
  their `agent-reflex.jsonc` is left untouched.
- The OpenCode side is NOT copied on updates: with the standard install the
  plugin lives in the opencode CLI's package install (`opencode plugin add
  github:psygreg/agent-reflex`), so the CLI tracks it (unpinned package
  plugins refresh on server startup; `opencode plugin update agent-reflex`
  forces it). A legacy local-copy install (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/reflex/`
  + a `"./plugins/reflex"` entry) IS migrated to the standard package, with
  its configured options carried over and the stale copy removed. In every
  case the configured classifier options are left untouched.
- If it instead prints the setup menu and ends with "No input available
  (stdin closed)", there is no installation yet — follow the fresh-install
  section below.
- After updating, **tell the user to restart OpenCode** (`opencode service
  restart`). Do not restart it yourself: it would terminate this session.

## Fresh install

The installer asks questions in a fixed order and reads the answers from
stdin, so collect them from the user in chat first, then pipe them in one
line each. The exact order:

1. Provider: `1` llamacpp, `2` ollama, `3` lmstudio, `4` typesafe,
   `5` openrouter, `6` vercel, `7` opencode (OpenCode Zen), `8` custom.
2. Providers 1-3 only: "Server runs on this machine?" — `Y` or `n`. If `n`,
   the next answer is the remote base URL including `/v1`
   (e.g. `http://192.168.1.10:8080/v1`). Provider 8 (custom) takes the base
   URL here directly.
3. Classifier model. An empty answer takes the preset default (`nimble`,
   `jev-latest`, `~typesafe/jev-latest`, `typesafe-ai/jev`, `jev-1.13`);
   required for llamacpp and lmstudio (their models are free-form ids).
4. API key, optional, `{env:NAME}` substitution supported and preferred over
   literal keys.
5. Fallback classifier model on the same endpoint, optional.
6. Debug log file path, optional.

Example — Jev through the TypeSafe API with the key from the environment:

```sh
printf '4\n\n{env:TYPESAFE_API_KEY}\n\n\n' | bash ../../../install.sh
```

(Colors are automatic and turn off by themselves when output is not a
terminal, so nothing extra is needed when running it from an agent.)

Fresh installs verify the classifier before writing anything: after the
answers are collected the installer asks the endpoint one real System One
question at `<baseURL>/systemone` and refuses to continue when the endpoint
does not answer with the System One decision shape (`answers.<id>.noul`, a
number in [0, 1]). A plain chat/completion server on the same port, an
outdated local runtime, a model that is not a decision model, a wrong port,
or the classic field mix-ups (the model name in the apiKey field, a bare
port as the baseURL, an api key identical to the model id) stop the install
with the exact fix named. When that happens, correct the answers with the
user and re-run — do NOT bypass the check (`AGENT_REFLEX_SKIP_VERIFY=1`)
unless the user asks for it and no other environment can reach the endpoint.

The plugin installs through the OpenCode plugin CLI itself as a standard
package (`opencode plugin add github:psygreg/agent-reflex`; the installer
runs it and then merges the classifier options into the entry the CLI
wrote). Older CLIs without the plugin command fall back to the legacy
local-copy layout — that fallback needs the merge (bun, node bundled with
npm or deno) for `opencode.json(c)`; without any of them the script prints
the entry for a manual paste — in that case, show the printed entry to the
user instead of editing the config blindly.

Report the script's `[agent-reflex]` messages to the user, confirm the merged
entry looks right, and remind them to restart OpenCode — again, do not run
`opencode service restart` from inside the session.

description: Ask the System One classifier to evaluate the current line of thought or draft solution and return a confidence verdict. Use before committing to a solution on a medium or high complexity task. Returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

# Confidence check

Evaluate the current line of thought or draft solution with the System One
classifier and follow its verdict.

1. Gather the current line of thought or draft solution as one block of text.
2. Run the confidence check script with that text:

   ```
   ./scripts/confidence.sh check
   ```

   Run it from the plugin root (the directory holding `agent-reflex.jsonc`), or
   pass an absolute path to the script. Pass the thought through stdin. The script
   returns a confidence percentage and a verdict.

3. Interpret the verdict:
   - **CONTINUE** — the line of thought is direct, correct, and without redundant
     loops. Proceed with it.
   - **RESTART** — the confidence is below the threshold for the current
     complexity level. Discard that line of thought and solve the problem again,
     focusing on the cleanest, most direct solution.

If the script reports the classifier is unavailable, continue with the current
approach and note that the check could not run.

Thresholds: simple 0.75, medium/high 0.85 (the plugin's default). The level is
read from the state the classify hook stored for this conversation; when absent
the simple threshold applies.

# agent-reflex
Plugin for coding agent workflow optimization and safeguarding using any system one decision model, from Jev to self-hosted LM Studio, Ollama or llama.cpp.

### Goals
- Safeguard against potentially dangerous shell commands
- Improve token efficiency
- Deliver more reliable solutions to tasks

### Requirement
The plugin needs a System One decision model as its classifier, served at
`<baseURL>/systemone` — local llama.cpp (0.6 onwards), Ollama (0.35 onwards) or
LM Studio (0.4.26 onwards), or TypeSafe Jev and other System One models through
the TypeSafe API, OpenRouter, the Vercel AI Gateway or OpenCode Zen. Every
feature below is driven by this classifier.

### Features
- **Skill suggestions**: on a conversation's initial prompt the classifier scores which skills available to the agent fit the task (one `noul` question per skill, riding the same batched request as the other decisions) and injects a short suggestion naming the top matches to load via the `skill` tool (OpenCode only — it reads the agent's skill registry). Follow-up prompts in the same conversation are not re-checked: the verdict settles on the task the conversation opens with, and the nudge stays visible only through that first request's turns, dropping a skill once the model has loaded it (a first turn the classifier could not answer leaves the check pending; the next prompt completes it). The suggestion stays silent when the catalog or the classifier is unavailable: it is optional help, never a blocker
- **Project agent-docs nudge**: repositories increasingly carry agent guidance at their root — an `AGENTS.md` file (the cross-agent convention, optionally also nested per subdirectory) or a `.ai/` directory. On a conversation's initial prompt the plugin checks the project directory for both and, when one exists, injects a one-line note telling the model to read it before starting the task (the files are pointed at, never inlined). The note rides the opening turn's model calls and is never fed again on later prompts of the same conversation, so the pointer is paid for once; the check is a filesystem stat, not a classifier decision (`agentDocs` option, OpenCode only)
- **Decision-driven history compaction**: keeps the recent messages verbatim (keep-window widens with complexity), keeps a bounded set of load-bearing older messages, and folds the rest into a compact structured digest so its detail is compressed rather than discarded. Folding is incremental: each compaction only summarizes the messages that aged out of the keep window since the last fold — batched (short turns stay cheap), folded once per session — and appends their facts to a persistent per-session long-term block, so per-request compaction cost stays roughly flat as the session grows and older facts stay captured instead of being redrawn away by every fresh digest run. Tool outputs, tool-call plumbing and thinking/reasoning blocks past the keep window are not even scored: they are discarded outright, since the assistant turns that interpreted them are the load-bearing content and old file reads or command dumps would otherwise spend the preserved slots and the classifier budget
- **Dynamic thinking effort level**: qualifies each prompt as *low*, *medium* or *high* complexity, setting `maxTokens` and switching reasoning effort when the agent uses the default effort setting. A non-default model variant or explicit effort option takes precedence. The request dialect is detected per request from the model actually being requested, so multimodel setups — including one gateway proxying many models — never send a foreign field; models without a wired dialect stay untouched and can still use other features of the plugin. Wired dialects: Anthropic, llama.cpp, Ollama, OpenAI GPT reasoning models, Z.ai GLM (GLM-5.2 onwards), Xiaomi MiMo (MiMo-V2.5 onwards), Google Gemini (Gemini 3 onwards), Qwen (Qwen3.5 onwards and the qwen-plus/qwen-max aliases), Moonshot Kimi (kimi-k2.7+/kimi-k3), xAI Grok (grok-4.3 onwards) and MiniMax (MiniMax-M3 onwards)
- **Confidence level tool**: automatically suggested for *medium* and *high* complexity tasks, allows the LLM to check the confidence of its current line of thinking before finalizing a response and correct itself along the way if needed
- **Tool exposure**: for each prompt the classifier decides which tool *groups* the task actually needs (tools are judged by purpose — web, shell, edit, read, agents, other — one question per group, not per tool) and the model is given only those, so the request carries fewer tool schemas and saves input tokens; a kept group keeps its whole family of tools. In OpenCode, request complexity, tool-group relevance, and history relevance are batched and reused across tool continuations, and history verdicts persist across requests (each old prose message is judged by the classifier at most once per session; tool outputs and reasoning blocks are never judged), while folded history is summarized incrementally into a long-term block, keeping long-session compaction latency low; simultaneous safety/edit checks are batched too. Sequential safety and edit checks remain per action because their inputs arrive only then. The always-keep set is the common core (read/search/edit/shell/task, plus the `execute`/`search`/`skill`/`question` meta-tools where the harness routes everything through them) plus `reflex_run`, `systemone_check_confidence` and `systemone_reveal_tools`. If a needed tool was trimmed, the latter lists the agent's tool pool and restores all tool schemas for the current user request. Falls back to exposing everything if the classifier is unavailable
- **Decision-model tool dispatch** (`reflex_run`): an optional fallback tool for when the model cannot decide which underlying tool a task needs. It asks the decision model which tool to use (a `choice` decision), runs it, and returns its real output. The model calls tools directly whenever it already knows which one fits and reaches for `reflex_run` only when the correct tool is unclear. Tool dispatch uses the same configured classifier model as the rest of the plugin
- **Syntax checks**: up to two-step checks after `edit` and `write` tool calls using parsers and the decision model
- **Shell guardrail**: blocks commands that may damage a repository or remove files without backup; the check runs before dispatch through `reflex_run` as well

- **Stuck-loop detection**: watches completed tool calls and breaks repetitive cycles. When the *same call keeps producing the same result* — identical arguments and identical output, several times in the last few calls — it is flagged deterministically as a stuck loop, no classifier involved, and a warning naming the repeated call and its evidence is injected into the next model call telling the model to change approach; a repeated call whose output *varies* is judged by the System One classifier instead (with a lower bar once the repetition is structurally proven, and the verdict cached per repeating pattern but re-judged as the loop grows). Detection is conservative so legitimate iteration passes through untouched: the warning is a nudge, never a stop, it is delivered once per loop and repeated only if the loop persists

### Agent support

Eight agents are supported. The classifier config is shared across all of them
(`agent-reflex.jsonc`, same option names), so the classifier questions are answered
once. Dynamic effort needs the plugin to rewrite the model request, and history
compaction needs it to rewrite the message list — both only reach agents whose hook
API allows that rewrite.

| Agent | Shell guardrail | Post-edit checks | Classify + confidence | Compaction guidance | Dynamic effort | History compaction | Tool exposure | Tool dispatch | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenCode** | ✅ hard block | ✅ inline | ✅ | ✅ built-in | ✅ full (per-model dialects) | ✅ decision-driven | ✅ | ✅ (`reflex_run`) | Reference implementation and the only agent where everything works. |
| **Pi** | ✅ hard block | ✅ inline | ✅ | ✅ via `context` | ✅ full (`setThinkingLevel`) | ✅ opt-in decision-driven | ✅ (`setActiveTools`) | ✅ (`reflex_run`) | Pi translates the unified effort level per model itself, so no per-vendor dialect code is needed. |
| **MiMo Code** | ✅ hard block | ✅ inline | ✅ | ✅ compacting hook | ⚠️ token cap only | ✅ opt-in decision-driven | ❌ | ❌ | OpenCode-derived. `chat.params` sets `maxTokens` but not `reasoning_effort`, so effort cannot change how hard the model thinks. |
| **Claude Code** | ✅ hard block | ✅ inline | ✅ | ✅ fact-extraction guidance | ❌ | ⚠️ digest guidance only | ❌ | ❌ | `PreCompact` reads the transcript and extracts the fact buckets to steer the summary, but hooks cannot rewrite the message list, so it cannot choose what to keep. |
| **Qwen Code** | ✅ hard block | ✅ inline | ✅ | ✅ fact-extraction guidance | ❌ | ⚠️ digest guidance only | ❌ | ❌ | Same hook limits as Claude Code. Strongest of the shell-hook ports. |
| **Codex** | ✅ hard block | ✅ inline | ✅ | ❌ inert | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | No `PreCompact` `custom_instructions`; its compaction hook can only cancel compaction. Edits arrive via `apply_patch` (V4A). |
| **Antigravity** | ✅ hard block | ⚠️ one turn late | ✅ | ❌ inert | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | `PostToolUse` cannot inject context (open upstream antigravity-cli#808), so findings queue and surface at the next model call. |
| **Hermes** | ⚠️ wrapper tool | ✅ inline | ✅ | ❌ none | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Hooks cannot block a tool call, so the guardrail is a `safe_run` wrapper over `terminal`. No compaction hook. |

Legend: ✅ works · ⚠️ works with a documented compromise · ❌ not possible (agent hook
API limitation). Dynamic effort means both the reasoning/thinking level and the
per-level `maxTokens` cap where the agent exposes one. Tool exposure means the
agent can remove tool schemas from the model's request (real input-token savings);
the shell-hook agents can only deny a tool call after the model already chose it,
which saves nothing and is therefore marked ❌.

## Usage
Install the skill using `npx skills add psygreg/agent-reflex` or `bun x skills add psygreg/agent-reflex` then ask your agent to do it: the skill briefs the agent on the plugin's capabilities and installs or updates it — updates need no answers (`bash install.sh </dev/null`), fresh installs collect the answers in chat and pipe them in.

Or run the install script provided in this repository. It will also install the skill so future updates can be performed through the agent itself.

```sh
./install.sh
```

On a fresh install it asks for the classifier provider (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, OpenCode Zen or a custom endpoint), whether a local server runs on the same machine or a remote one (with its base URL), the classifier model, an optional API key (`{env:NAME}` supported), an optional fallback classifier model and an optional debug log path. Then it verifies the answers against the server itself before writing anything: the collected endpoint must answer a real System One question at `<baseURL>/systemone` with the configured model, and every field is checked against the mis-fills that leave the plugin broken silently (the model name in the apiKey field, a bare port as the baseURL, an api key identical to the model) — a plain chat or completion server on the same port is refused with the exact reason. `AGENT_REFLEX_SKIP_VERIFY=1` bypasses this probe for environments it cannot reach.

The OpenCode plugin installs through the OpenCode plugin CLI: `install.sh` runs `opencode plugin add github:psygreg/agent-reflex` (or `opencode plugin <spec> -g` on older CLIs), so the plugin lives in the CLI's own package install and the entry lands in the global config the standard way; the classifier options are merged into that entry (`{ "package": "github:psygreg/agent-reflex", "options": { ... } }`, keeping comments and formatting; a `.agent-reflex.bak` backup is kept next to the config and the merged file is validated before committing). Older CLIs without the standard plugin command, offline machines, or a missing JS runtime fall back to the legacy local-copy layout (`plugins/reflex` next to the config + a `./plugins/reflex` entry) — re-running the installer on such an installation migrates it to the standard package install. The skill installs through the skills CLI (`bunx`/`npx skills add`, into the CLI's own canonical path) when no copy exists yet; existing copies are detected and left untouched, so there is never a second installation path.

Re-running the installer only updates the plugin: an existing installation (standard package, legacy copy or config entry) is detected and the configured options are left untouched — except that a legacy local-copy install migrates to the standard package install, with its options carried over. Each part installs only for the software actually present: the OpenCode plugin and its `opencode.json(c)` entry are written only when the `opencode` CLI is on `PATH`, and each agent port (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Qwen Code, Antigravity, Pi, MiMo Code) only when that agent's CLI is present — anything you do not have installed is skipped entirely, with no files or config written for it. If none of the supported agents is installed, a fresh install stops before the classifier prompts and reports that there is nothing to install. After installing or updating, restart OpenCode (`opencode service restart`) to load the plugin.

For development, add a `"debugLog":` key to the plugin's options pointing to a file to write the logs into. Configuration reference examples live in `opencode.example.jsonc`.

- Add automatic effort changing capabilities for local models running through LM Studio (blocked upstream: its OpenAI-compatible endpoint documents no reasoning field yet)
- Add automatic effort changing capabilities for other providers beyond the wired dialects (Anthropic, GPT, GLM, MiMo, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi, Grok, MiniMax)

# agent-reflex for Antigravity

Antigravity port of the `agent-reflex` OpenCode plugin: a small System One decision
model runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check edits, and
let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

This is an Antigravity plugin (`plugin.json` + `hooks/hooks.json` + `scripts/` + a
`confidence` skill). Install it into the global plugin dir
(`~/.gemini/config/plugins/agent-reflex/`) or the workspace `.agents/plugins/`, and
create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root with your classifier settings.

## What it does

- **Shell guardrail** (`PreToolUse` on `run_command`): scores a command for damage
  potential and denies it (`decision: "deny"`, a hard block) when the score exceeds
  the threshold. On classifier failure the command is allowed.
- **Post-edit double-check** (`PostToolUse` on `write_to_file` /
  `replace_file_content` / `multi_replace_file_content`): runs a language parser on
  the edited file and, on medium/high complexity tasks, a System One bug check on
  the edited text. Findings are delivered to the model on the next invocation (see
  "The one-turn delay" below).
- **Complexity classification** (`PreInvocation`): scores the current prompt
  *simple*/*medium*/*high* (read from the transcript) and, on medium/high, injects a
  note suggesting a confidence check.
- **Confidence check** (`confidence` skill): scores the model's current line of
  thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## The one-turn delay (the Antigravity post-edit compromise)

Antigravity's `PostToolUse` hook **cannot inject context the model sees** — its
stdout contract is an empty `{}`, and its payload omits the successful tool output
(an open upstream request: antigravity-cli#808). So the post-edit check runs in two
phases instead of feeding findings back inline with the edit:

1. `PostToolUse` runs the syntax/bug check and appends findings to a per-conversation
   pending file (the edited file is re-read from disk, since the payload has no
   output).
2. `PreInvocation` (the next model call) delivers those findings via `injectSteps`
   and clears the file.

This means the model sees a syntax error or bug warning one turn after the edit
rather than as part of the edit's tool result. It is the closest approximation
available until Antigravity adds `PostToolUse` context injection. Everything else
(guardrail, classification, confidence) is unaffected.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, the hooks that need the classifier fail open:
the shell command runs, the edit passes, and the confidence check reports the
classifier is unavailable.

## Antigravity-only compromises (features not portable here)

The OpenCode plugin rewrites the model request itself (`http.request`) and prunes
history (`context`). Antigravity exposes neither, so:

- **Per-request dynamic effort and `maxTokens`.** Impossible. No Antigravity hook
  can touch the request or set a per-request token cap. The classifier still
  classifies complexity, but only to drive the confidence suggestion and post-edit
  check depth.
- **Custom history pruning.** Impossible. Hooks can inject context (`injectSteps`)
  but cannot return a pruned message list. Antigravity owns compaction; the plugin
  can only add a preserve-requirements reminder, not drop messages.
- **Compaction steering.** No `PreCompact` `custom_instructions` lever exists (that
  is Claude Code/Qwen Code). The `compact.sh` hook is inert by default; set
  `AGENT_REFLEX_COMPACT_NOTE=1` to queue a preserve-requirements reminder alongside
  edit findings. Weaker than Claude Code/Qwen Code, comparable to Codex.

If you need those features, use the OpenCode plugin (`plugins/opencode`).

## Layout

```
plugin.json        manifest (name, description, schema)
hooks/hooks.json   hook registration (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation x2, PostInvocation)
scripts/common.sh  config + System One classifier client + helpers
scripts/guard.sh   shell guardrail (PreToolUse, decision: deny)
scripts/check.sh   post-edit syntax + bug check (PostToolUse check / PreInvocation deliver)
scripts/classify.sh  complexity classification (PreInvocation)
scripts/compact.sh   compaction note (PostInvocation, inert by default)
scripts/confidence.sh  on-demand confidence check (skill)
skills/confidence/SKILL.md  the confidence skill
```

# agent-reflex for Claude Code

Claude Code port of the `agent-reflex` OpenCode plugin: a small System One
decision model runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check
edits, and let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

This is a Claude Code plugin (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `hooks/hooks.json` +
`scripts/` + a `confidence` skill). Install it from a marketplace or load the
directory directly. After installing, create `agent-reflex.jsonc` next to the
plugin (in the plugin root) with your classifier settings.

## What it does

- **Shell guardrail** (`PreToolUse` on Bash): scores a command for damage
  potential and denies it when the score exceeds the threshold.
- **Post-edit double-check** (`PostToolUse` on Edit|Write): runs a language
  parser on the edited file and, on medium/high complexity tasks, a System One
  bug check on the lines around the edit. Failures are fed back to the agent to
  fix; a second failure on the same file asks the user how to proceed.
- **Complexity classification** (`UserPromptSubmit`): scores each prompt
  *simple*/*medium*/*high* and, on medium/high, suggests a confidence check.
- **Compaction guidance with fact extraction** (`PreCompact`): reads the
  conversation transcript (`transcript_path`), extracts the facts it established
  (goal, architecture, decisions, files, verification, and the other digest
  buckets) with the classifier, and steers Claude Code's own summarizer via
  `custom_instructions` to preserve them. Falls back to enriched static guidance
  when the transcript is unavailable. Guidance only — it cannot choose what to
  keep, just what the summary preserves.
- **Confidence check** (`/confidence` skill): scores the model's current line of
  thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, the hooks that need the classifier fail
open: the shell command runs, the edit passes, and the confidence check reports
the classifier is unavailable.

## OpenCode-only features (not portable to Claude Code)

The OpenCode plugin uses the `http.request` and `context` hooks to rewrite the
model request itself. Claude Code does not expose those, so two features have no
equivalent here and are intentionally omitted:

- **Per-request dynamic effort and `maxTokens`.** The OpenCode plugin rewrites
  every request's effort/thinking fields and token cap based on the classified
  complexity. Claude Code sets the effort level once per session (via `/effort`,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, or the model picker); hooks cannot change it
  mid-session or per request (model/effort changes require the manual `/model`
  picker — see claude-code issue #30806). The classifier still classifies
  complexity here, but only to drive the confidence suggestion and the post-edit
  check depth, not the request.
- **Decision-driven history compaction.** The OpenCode plugin keeps/drops messages
  and folds the tail into a digest before each model call. Claude Code owns
  compaction and does not let a hook rewrite the conversation history, so this
  plugin cannot select what to keep. It approximates the digest step instead:
  `PreCompact` reads the transcript, extracts the same fact buckets, and biases the
  summary to preserve them via `custom_instructions`.

If you need those two features, use the OpenCode plugin (`plugins/opencode`).

## Layout

```
.claude-plugin/plugin.json   manifest
hooks/hooks.json             hook registration (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact)
scripts/common.sh            config + System One classifier client + helpers
scripts/guard.sh             shell guardrail (PreToolUse)
scripts/check.sh             post-edit syntax + bug check (PostToolUse)
scripts/classify.sh          complexity classification (UserPromptSubmit)
scripts/compact.sh           compaction guidance (PreCompact)
scripts/confidence.sh        on-demand confidence check (skill)
skills/confidence/SKILL.md   the /confidence command
```

model runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check edits,
and let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

  System One bug check on the added lines. Codex edits files through
  `apply_patch`, so the hook parses the edited paths from the V4A patch.
  Failures are fed back to the agent to fix; a second failure on the same file
  asks the user how to proceed.
- **Complexity classification** (`UserPromptSubmit`): scores each prompt
  *simple*/*medium*/*high* and, on medium/high, suggests a confidence check.
- **Confidence check** (`/confidence` skill): scores the model's current line of
  thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, the hooks that need the classifier fail
open: the shell command runs, the edit passes, and the confidence check reports
the classifier is unavailable.

## Codex-only compromises (features not portable here)

The OpenCode plugin uses the `http.request` and `context` hooks to rewrite the
model request itself, and Claude Code adds a `PreCompact` `custom_instructions`
lever. Codex exposes neither, so three features are reduced or omitted:

- **Per-request dynamic effort and `maxTokens`.** The OpenCode plugin rewrites
  every request's effort/thinking fields and token cap from the classified
  complexity. Codex has no hook to touch the request or set a per-request token
  cap; `model_reasoning_effort` is a session-level config value. The classifier
  still classifies complexity here, but only to drive the confidence suggestion
  and the post-edit check depth. (Same limitation as Claude Code.)
- **Custom history pruning.** The OpenCode plugin prunes old messages before each
  model call. Codex owns compaction and offers no hook to rewrite history or steer
  what the summary keeps.
- **Compaction guidance.** Claude Code can bias compaction via `PreCompact`
  `custom_instructions`. Codex's `PreCompact` output is only
  `continue`/`stopReason`/`systemMessage`/`suppressOutput` — there is no way to
  tell the summarizer what to preserve. The only lever is `continue:false` to
  cancel compaction, which is rarely desirable. So this port's `PreCompact` hook
  is inert by default (it just logs the trigger) and, with
  `AGENT_REFLEX_COMPACT_NOTE=1`, surfaces a preserve-requirements reminder as a
  `systemMessage`. This is the weakest of the three ports for compaction.

If you need those features, use the OpenCode plugin (`plugins/opencode`).

## Codex hook notes

- Hooks are experimental in Codex and require trust review: run `/hooks` in the
  CLI to review and trust the bundled hook definitions before they run. For
  automation, `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` skips persisted trust.
- File edits arrive via `apply_patch`, so the post-edit check parses the V4A
  patch (`*** Update File:` / `*** Add File:` headers) to find edited paths. A
  direct `tool_input.file_path` is used when a tool supplies one.
- Matchers use Codex tool names: `Bash`, and `Edit|Write|apply_patch` for edits.

# agent-reflex for Hermes

Hermes port of the `agent-reflex` OpenCode plugin: a small System One decision
model runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check edits,
and let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

This is a Hermes plugin (`plugin.yaml` + `classifier.py` + `syntax.py` +
`__init__.py`). Install it into `~/.hermes/plugins/agent-reflex/`, enable it under
`plugins.enabled` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (the installer does both), and create
`agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root with your classifier settings.

## What it does

- **`safe_run` command wrapper** (the guardrail): a shell-execution tool that
  scores a command for damage potential with the classifier and either blocks it
  (returns an error) or runs it by delegating to Hermes's built-in `terminal` tool.
  Use `safe_run` instead of the plain `terminal` tool to get commands checked
  before they execute. See "Why a wrapper" below.
- **Post-edit double-check** (`post_tool_call`): after a file edit (`patch`,
  `write_file`, …) it runs a language parser on the file and, on medium/high
  complexity tasks, a System One bug check on the edited text. Findings are
  injected back to the agent to fix.
- **Complexity classification** (`pre_llm_call`): scores each prompt
  *simple*/*medium*/*high*, stores it for the session, and on medium/high injects
  a note suggesting a confidence check. This is the cleanest of all the ports —
  `pre_llm_call` can return context to append to the turn.
- **Confidence check** (`confidence_check` tool and `/confidence` command): scores
  the model's current line of thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## Why a wrapper (the Hermes guardrail compromise)

The shell ports (Claude Code, Codex) block a dangerous command in a `PreToolUse`
hook. Hermes's `pre_tool_call` hook **cannot block** — its return value is ignored
(it is a fire-and-forget observer, good for warnings only). To get a real block,
this port delivers the guardrail as a command-execution wrapper tool:

- The model calls `safe_run` with a command. The wrapper scores it, and:
  - score above the threshold → returns `{"error": "[GUARDRAIL BLOCKED] …"}` and
    never runs it (a real block);
  - otherwise → delegates to the built-in `terminal` tool via `ctx.dispatch_tool`,
    so approvals, credentials, and task context are preserved.
- A `pre_tool_call` hook prints a warning whenever a command runs through the
  plain `terminal` tool instead of `safe_run`, nudging the model toward the
  guarded path.

The compromise: enforcement depends on the model choosing `safe_run`. A model
that calls `terminal` directly bypasses the guardrail (it only gets a warning).
For hard enforcement, disable the `terminal` toolset so `safe_run` is the only
command path, or use Hermes's `terminal` backend sandbox (`docker`/`ssh`) as the
real boundary. The guardrail is best-effort by design, matching the plugin's
"never block work when the classifier is down" fail-open behavior.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, the hooks that need the classifier fail
open: commands run, edits pass, and the confidence check reports the classifier is
unavailable.

## Hermes-only compromises (features not portable here)

The OpenCode plugin rewrites the model request itself (`http.request`) and prunes
history (`context`). Hermes exposes neither, so:

- **Per-request dynamic effort and `maxTokens`.** Impossible. No Hermes hook can
  touch the request or set a per-request token cap. The classifier still classifies
  complexity, but only to drive the confidence suggestion and post-edit check depth.
- **Custom history pruning.** Only partial. `pre_llm_call` receives
  `conversation_history`, so the classifier could read it — but the hook can only
  return `{"context": …}` to append text; it cannot return a pruned message list.
  So Hermes can see history but cannot drop tokens. Real pruning is impossible.
- **Compaction guidance.** No compaction hook exists; Hermes does context
  compression internally and does not expose what it keeps. Weaker than Claude
  Code's `PreCompact custom_instructions`, comparable to Codex.

If you need those features, use the OpenCode plugin (`plugins/opencode`).

## Layout

```
plugin.yaml        manifest (name, version, description)
classifier.py      config loader (agent-reflex.jsonc) + System One client
syntax.py          language parsers + edit excerpt (post-edit check)
__init__.py        register(ctx): safe_run tool, hooks, confidence tool/command
```

# agent-reflex for MiMo Code

MiMo Code port of the `agent-reflex` OpenCode plugin: a small System One decision
model runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check edits, cap
tokens per task, compact history, and let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

MiMo Code is Xiaomi's own agent, and it is **OpenCode-derived** — `@mimo-ai/plugin`
is nearly identical to `@opencode-ai/plugin`. So this port is the lowest-effort of the
set, and it is the **second** (after Pi) where the two features every shell-based port
lacks actually work: custom history compaction and per-request `maxTokens`. Install the
hook files into your MiMo Code hooks dir and create `agent-reflex.jsonc` alongside
them with your classifier settings.

## What it does

- **Shell guardrail** (`tool.execute.before`): scores a command for damage potential
  and blocks it (`output.cancel = true`) before it runs. A real block.
- **Post-edit double-check** (`tool.execute.after`): runs a language parser on the
  edited file and, on medium/high complexity, a System One bug check on the edited
  text. Findings are appended to the tool result (`output.output`) — inline, unlike
  Antigravity's one-turn delay.
- **Complexity classification** (`experimental.chat.system.transform`): scores each
  prompt *simple*/*medium*/*high*, stores the level for the session, and on
  medium/high adds a note suggesting a confidence check to the system prompt.
- **Per-request `maxTokens`** (`chat.params`): sets the generated-token cap per level
  (simple 8192 / medium 65536 / high 131072), matching the plugin's caps.
- **Decision-driven history compaction** (`experimental.chat.messages.transform`,
  opt-in): when the history grows long, keeps the recent tail verbatim (window sized
  by complexity level), keeps a bounded set of high-relevance older messages verbatim,
  and folds the rest into a structured digest — buckets (goal, architecture,
  constraints, decisions, files, …) whose most representative sentence is picked by
  the classifier's `choice` primitive. Compresses rather than discards.
- **Compaction guidance** (`experimental.session.compacting`): steers the compaction
  summary to keep architectural requirements, scope, and rules.
- **Confidence check** (`confidence_check` custom tool): scores the model's current
  line of thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## The one caveat: effort is `maxTokens`-only

MiMo Code's `chat.params` hook exposes `temperature`, `topP`, and `maxOutputTokens` —
but **not** `reasoning_effort` or `thinking`. MiMo's own reasoning knob is
`reasoning.effort` on the wire (`none`/`low`/`medium`/`high`), which is not reachable
from hooks. So on MiMo Code the plugin's "dynamic effort" feature is the **token cap
only**; it cannot change how hard the model thinks. (Pi, by contrast, exposes
`setThinkingLevel()` and does map effort properly.) The system-prompt confidence hint
is the only soft nudge toward more careful reasoning. This is a MiMo Code limitation,
not a plugin one.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` next to the hook files. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, every hook fails open: the shell command runs,
the edit passes, the cap is left alone, and the confidence check reports the
classifier is unavailable.

## Feature flags

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `AGENT_REFLEX_PRUNE=1` | Enable decision-driven history compaction (`experimental.chat.messages.transform`). One classifier call per old message plus one batched digest call per model request — real latency/token cost. Off by default. |

The guardrail, post-edit check, classification, `maxTokens` cap, and compaction
guidance are always on.

## Install

MiMo Code loads **file hooks** from `hooks/*.ts` (compiled with Bun.build, hot-reloaded).
The `plugin` array in config does NOT execute module code — a documented gotcha — so
this port ships as hook files, not a plugin entry. Copy them into your hooks dir:

- global: `~/.config/mimocode/hooks/` (or `~/.mimocode/hooks/`)
- project: `.mimocode/hooks/`

Files: `index.ts` (the hook module), `classifier.ts`, `check.ts`. The confidence tool
(`tools.ts`) goes in `.mimocode/tools/`.

## Layout

```
index.ts         the hook module (six hooks: chat.params, messages/system transform, tool.execute.before/after, session.compacting)
classifier.ts    config loader (agent-reflex.jsonc) + System One client + level map
check.ts         language parsers + edit excerpt (post-edit check)
tools.ts         confidence_check custom tool
test.ts          behavior tests (not installed)
```

# agent-reflex for Pi

Pi port of the `agent-reflex` OpenCode plugin: a small System One decision model
runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check edits, tune
effort per task, compact history, and let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

Pi is the most extensible agent this plugin ports to, and the **only one** where
the two OpenCode-only features on every other port actually work: dynamic effort
and decision-driven history compaction. Install it into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/agent-reflex/`
(the installer does this), and create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root with
your classifier settings.

## What it does

- **Dynamic thinking effort** (`before_agent_start`): classifies each prompt
  *simple*/*medium*/*high* and sets Pi's native thinking level
  (`off`/`low`/`high`) with `pi.setThinkingLevel()`. Pi translates the unified
  level to each model's native wire field via its own `thinkingLevelMap`, so this
  replaces the OpenCode plugin's hand-rolled per-vendor dialects (GLM, MiMo,
  Gemini, Qwen, Kimi, Grok, MiniMax…). This is the plugin's headline feature and it works
  at full fidelity here.
- **Decision-driven history compaction** (`context`, opt-in): when the history
  grows long, keeps the recent messages verbatim (a keep-window that widens with
  complexity), keeps a bounded set of load-bearing older messages, and folds the
  rest into a compact structured digest of the facts they established — so detail
  is compressed rather than discarded. Structural (tool call/result) messages are
  scored like any other and only survive when load-bearing. The `context` event
  receives a deep copy of the message list and can return a rewritten one — the
  one capability no other non-OpenCode agent exposes.
- **Shell guardrail** (`tool_call`): scores a command for damage potential and
  blocks it (`{ block: true }`) before it runs. A real block, like Claude
  Code/Codex/Qwen Code/Antigravity.
- **Post-edit double-check** (`tool_result`): runs a language parser on the edited
  file and, on medium/high complexity, a System One bug check on the edited text.
  Findings are appended to the tool result so the agent can fix problems.
- **Complexity classification** (`before_agent_start`): also injects a note
  suggesting a confidence check on medium/high.
- **Tool exposure** (`before_agent_start`): decides which tool *groups* the
  task needs (tools are judged by purpose — web, shell, edit, read, agents,
  other — one question per group, not per tool) and narrows the active set with
  `pi.setActiveTools()`, so the request carries fewer tool schemas and saves
  input tokens; a kept group keeps its whole family of tools. The always-keep
  set is the common core (read/search/edit/shell/task) plus `reflex_run`, so the
  model keeps the direct tools it reaches for constantly and only the long tail
  (web, exec,
  subagents…) is trimmed to what the task clearly needs or the model already used
  this session. Everything stays exposed if the classifier is
  unavailable. Disable with `AGENT_REFLEX_TOOLS=0`.
- **Tool dispatch** (`reflex_run` tool): an optional fallback for when the model
  cannot decide which underlying tool a task needs. It asks the decision model
  which tool to use (a `choice` decision), runs it via `ctx.executeTool`, and
  returns its real output. The model calls tools directly whenever it already
  knows which one fits and reaches for `reflex_run` only when the correct tool is
  unclear. The shell guardrail runs before dispatch. Tool dispatch uses the same
  configured classifier model.
- **Confidence check** (`confidence_check` tool and `/confidence` command): scores
  the model's current line of thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, the hooks that need the classifier fail
open: the shell command runs, the edit passes, effort is left alone, and the
confidence check reports the classifier is unavailable.

## Feature flags

Two features carry real cost or override provider defaults, so they are opt-in:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `AGENT_REFLEX_PRUNE=1` | Enable decision-driven history compaction (`context`). One classifier call per old message plus one batched digest call per model request — real latency and token cost. Off by default. |
| `AGENT_REFLEX_MAXTOKENS=1` | Set the request token cap per level (`before_provider_request`), matching the plugin's `maxTokens` (simple 8192, medium 65536, high 131072). Overrides the provider's own cap. Off by default. |
| `AGENT_REFLEX_TOOLS=0` | Disable tool exposure. When set to `0` (or `all`), every tool stays exposed. On by default (`auto`); makes one classifier batch call per prompt to score the tool groups. |

The effort tuning, guardrail, post-edit check, and confidence check are always on.

## Level mapping

Complexity maps to Pi's thinking level as `simple→off`, `medium→low`,
`high→high` — the "simple disables thinking" convention used for the MiMo and
Qwen ports. Pi clamps the level to the active model's `thinkingLevelMap`, so a
model that cannot reach `off` (some reasoning models are always on) falls to its
nearest supported level rather than erroring.

## Pi-only notes

- **Effort and pruning are fully portable here** — the two features every other
  non-OpenCode port documents as impossible. Pi's `setThinkingLevel()` and the
  `context` event's `{ messages }` return make them native.
- **Per-model effort dialects are delegated to Pi.** The OpenCode plugin maintains
  hand-rolled rewrites (`applyZaiLevel`, `applyMimoLevel`, `applyGeminiLevel`, …);
  on Pi that layer is `thinkingLevelMap`, which Pi already keeps per-model correct.
- **Pruning cost.** The `context` handler scores each old message with the
  classifier before every model request. That is faithful to the OpenCode plugin
  but can be slow on long histories — hence the `AGENT_REFLEX_PRUNE=1` gate. A
  future improvement is to batch or cache scores.
- Extensions run in-process with full permissions (like Hermes), so there is no
  sandbox boundary beyond what you add.

## Layout

```
index.ts         the extension factory (registers events, the tool, the command)
classifier.ts    config loader (agent-reflex.jsonc) + System One client
check.ts         language parsers + edit excerpt (post-edit check)
test.ts          behavior tests (not installed)
```

# agent-reflex for Qwen Code

Qwen Code port of the `agent-reflex` OpenCode plugin: a small System One decision
model runs alongside the agent to safeguard shell commands, double-check edits,
and let the model sanity-check its own reasoning.

This is a Qwen Code extension (`qwen-extension.json` + `hooks/` + `scripts/` + a
`confidence` skill). Install it with `qwen extensions install <dir>` (or copy it to
`~/.qwen/extensions/agent-reflex/`), and create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin
root with your classifier settings.

## What it does

- **Shell guardrail** (`PreToolUse` on `run_shell_command`): scores a command for
  damage potential and denies it (`permissionDecision: "deny"`) when the score
  exceeds the threshold. A hard block, like Claude Code and Codex.
- **Post-edit double-check** (`PostToolUse` on `write_file`/`edit`/`notebook_edit`):
  runs a language parser on the edited file and, on medium/high complexity tasks, a
  System One bug check on the edited text. Findings are injected as tool-result
  context so the agent can fix problems. Qwen's `write_file` uses `file_path` +
  `content` and `edit` uses `file_path` + `old_string` + `new_string`; the hook
  reads both shapes.
- **Complexity classification** (`UserPromptSubmit`): scores each prompt
  *simple*/*medium*/*high* and, on medium/high, injects a note suggesting a
  confidence check.
- **Compaction guidance with fact extraction** (`PreCompact`): reads the
  conversation transcript (`transcript_path`), extracts the facts it established
  (goal, architecture, decisions, files, verification, and the other digest
  buckets) with the classifier, and steers Qwen Code's own summarizer via
  `custom_instructions` to preserve them. Falls back to enriched static guidance
  when the transcript is unavailable. Qwen Code supports the same `PreCompact`
  `custom_instructions` lever as Claude Code. Guidance only — it cannot choose what
  to keep, just what the summary preserves.
- **Confidence check** (`confidence` skill, invocable as `/agent-reflex:confidence`):
  scores the model's current line of thought and returns CONTINUE or RESTART.

## Configuration

Create `agent-reflex.jsonc` in the plugin root. Option names match the OpenCode
plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": "llamacpp",          // llamacpp | ollama | lmstudio | typesafe | openrouter | vercel | opencode | custom
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",  // optional; overrides the preset
  "model": "liquid-d1",            // REQUIRED classifier model
  "apiKey": "{env:MY_API_KEY}",    // optional; {env:NAME} is resolved
  "fallbackModel": "jev-1.13",     // optional; retried when the primary rejects
  "debugLog": "/tmp/agent-reflex.log"  // optional
}
```

When `model` or `baseURL` is missing, the hooks that need the classifier fail
open: the shell command runs, the edit passes, and the confidence check reports
the classifier is unavailable.

## Qwen Code-only compromises (features not portable here)

The OpenCode plugin uses the `http.request` and `context` hooks to rewrite the
model request itself. Qwen Code exposes neither, so two features stay OpenCode-only
(same as every non-OpenCode port):

- **Per-request dynamic effort and `maxTokens`.** No Qwen Code hook can rewrite
  the request or set a per-request token cap. The classifier still classifies
  complexity, but only to drive the confidence suggestion and post-edit check depth.
- **Decision-driven history compaction.** Hooks can inject context but cannot
  return a rewritten message list, so this plugin cannot select what to keep. Qwen
  Code owns compaction (`/compress`, `PreCompact`); the plugin approximates the
  digest step instead — `PreCompact` reads the transcript, extracts the same fact
  buckets, and biases the summary to preserve them.

If you need those features, use the OpenCode plugin (`plugins/opencode`).

## Layout

```
qwen-extension.json       manifest (name, version, description)
hooks/hooks.json          hook registration (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact)
scripts/common.sh         config + System One classifier client + helpers
scripts/guard.sh          shell guardrail (PreToolUse, denies dangerous commands)
scripts/check.sh          post-edit syntax + bug check (PostToolUse)
scripts/classify.sh       complexity classification (UserPromptSubmit)
scripts/compact.sh        compaction guidance (PreCompact custom_instructions)
scripts/confidence.sh     on-demand confidence check (skill)
skills/confidence/SKILL.md  the confidence skill
```
